objective: Determine whether YYImage-derived APNG semantic replay reset points can reduce or eliminate retained full-canvas checkpoints without increasing retained or modeled peak bytes, while preserving fail-closed controls where source/disposal semantics do not establish an independent replay start.
modelBoundary: Semantic replay starts are derived from the exact retained YYImage 1.0.4 _updateSourceAPNG blendFromIndex/lastBlendIndex rules and source-bound ImageCraft frame rect/blend/disposal metadata.

A full-canvas background-disposal frame may advance the next replay anchor only according to the YYImage source algorithm; subrect background disposal is a negative control and must not receive the same reset.
A full-canvas source-blend frame establishes an independent replay start at its own index unless disposal is previous; subrect source frames do not establish a full-canvas replay reset.
The study is analytical. It excludes allocator fragmentation, decode latency, CPU, energy, thermal behavior, physical-device pressure, framework-private state, and production integration.
The existing FOVEA-W5-APNG-CHECKPOINT-MODEL-V1 report remains unchanged. This plan evaluates an additive semantic-reset model and must not rewrite prior preregistered evidence.

claimBoundary.allowed: scoped analytical Pareto statements when retained bytes and modeled peak bytes are equal or lower and replay metrics are strictly lower for the same source-derived scenario
claimBoundary.forbidden: runtime, device, energy, thermal, universal APNG, or global library superiority claims
